headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad network/API and API-key handling create dangerous default leakage and action-cascade risks; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower because Awesome Python is non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Awesome Python is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Firecrawl output by default. Firecrawl can emit web content and markdown, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. Any injection pathway would require unusual manual copy/paste or external wiring, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Firecrawl output into a downstream prompt or file consumed by another agent, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added between the pair, prompt content can traverse automatically.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not pipe Firecrawl output into any prompt without review.
Use a strict markdown-to-text sanitizer before any manual transfer.
Disable clipboard-based handoff during review sessions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted prompt templates for downstream consumers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Awesome Python touches no data classes and has no network egress, while Firecrawl touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys and can call external APIs. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but Firecrawl’s broad egress means any copied artifacts or shared files could leak sensitive material if introduced. The pathway exists in default Firecrawl usage, though not from Awesome Python alone.
conditions: IF Firecrawl is given files or prompts containing secrets, those contents may be transmitted to third-party endpoints.
IF both agents are placed in a shared workspace, copied artifacts can be exposed to Firecrawl's API calls.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any Firecrawl input.
Run Firecrawl with a redacted test dataset first.
Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Rotate any API keys used in Firecrawl after testing.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Awesome Python has no write or network surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad API use, but without a shared writable target there is no meaningful overlap. The pairwise conflict is therefore limited unless an operator adds a common filesystem, git repo, or OAuth scope.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or git repository, write conflicts become possible.
IF Firecrawl is granted the same OAuth scope as another writer, mutable-resource contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep Awesome Python read-only and non-executing.
Assign Firecrawl a separate output directory.
Avoid shared git branches for generated artifacts.
Use per-run subfolders for Firecrawl outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Awesome Python can serve as a reference source, and Firecrawl can scrape, crawl, and interact with web content, so Firecrawl may act on or render outputs derived from upstream material. Because Firecrawl has downstream action-taking capability via APIs and interactive scraping, unverified upstream facts can cascade into incorrect extraction or automation. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Firecrawl consumes text or URLs produced from Awesome Python without verification, upstream errors can propagate.
IF Firecrawl is used to automate scraping or interaction based on those outputs, incorrect facts can trigger wrong actions.
mitigations: Verify upstream facts before passing them to Firecrawl.
Use a human review step for any generated URLs or selectors.
Compare Firecrawl outputs against a second source.
Log source provenance alongside each derived artifact.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Awesome Python is a static open-source collection with no data classes touched, so it does not itself create residency or retention issues. Firecrawl, however, handles web content, screenshots, and API keys and may transmit them through its API endpoints. The pair only raises compliance concerns if regulated data is introduced into Firecrawl; the other agent is not a compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are sent to Firecrawl, retention and residency obligations may apply.
IF Firecrawl is used on EU or PHI data without a matching DPA or HIPAA posture, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to Firecrawl.
Review Firecrawl retention settings before use.
Use synthetic data for testing.
Document the data class allowed for each run.
requires-engineering: add policy checks before API submission.
